decision: Deploy KonnectYatra to production at konnectyatra.org using a symlinked public_html -> ~/konnectyatra/public, with GitHub Actions SSH auto-deploy on push to main
reasoning: Main-domain docroot is locked to public_html; symlink keeps app code out of the web root and URLs clean. Host has SSH+Composer, so Actions-over-SSH gives true push-to-deploy without exposing tokens in the repo.
expected_outcome: Pushing to main updates the live site in ~30s with no manual steps; data seeded from local XAMPP dump

decision: Rebuilt the Yatri booking flow: 19 airport-based Gurpurab packages from the pricing sheet (old ones disabled via new package.status column), cascading origin selector, fuller apply form (nationality, WebP doc uploads, yatri_documents table), admin-configured Payment Settings shown on the payment page, Pay Later email + 30-day validity, unique date/time Yatri IDs, and Yatri Booking Form print/PDF export (dompdf + FPDI)
reasoning: Client supplied the airport pricing sheet and booking-form design; needed accurate per-origin packages, complete applicant records, configurable payment instructions, and printable/exportable booking forms bundling uploaded documents
expected_outcome: Bookings capture full data with unique IDs; staff can configure payments and export complete Yatri forms with documents; new schema/seed/deps must be applied on production at deploy

decision: Bundle a 42,741-row US ZIP table in the repo instead of calling a live ZIP lookup API
reasoning: Gurdwara ZIP search and the Address Book both need ZIP -> city/coords. A free API (zippopotam.us) needs no setup but makes a public production page depend on a third party staying up. A bundled CSV + seeder costs 1.45MB in git and one prod seed command, and is then instant and offline-proof.
expected_outcome: ZIP search and Address Book keep working regardless of any third-party outage; no API keys or billing to manage

decision: Use keyless Google Maps links for the Address Book rather than the paid Places API
reasoning: Rashad needs to find gurdwaras that are not yet in the database while in the field. Places API auto-flags what is missing but needs a Google Cloud key with billing (~$32/1k searches); a Maps search button centred on his GPS plus the normal Add form costs nothing and ships immediately.
expected_outcome: Rashad can still discover and add missing gurdwaras on site, at zero cost; revisit only if manual adding proves too slow

decision: Merge the client gurdwara sheet onto existing rows and keep extras, rather than replacing the table
reasoning: The 151-row sheet has no photos or sangat sizes, abbreviated names ('Gurd ...') and typos, and only 33 of the 43 existing rows matched it. A straight replace would have destroyed 17 photos and put typo'd names on the public site.
expected_outcome: 43 -> 150 gurdwaras with all photos and sangat data intact; blank sheet cells never overwrite good stored values
